pr.title: Put the command first on project's command line
pr.head: 189eef5efc4da61714879e18690342dfa3f1a5ba

summary: project init writes Claude Code permission rules into the person's own settings: Bash(project *) allows every project command, and ask rules such as Bash(project init *) make Claude Code ask before the few commands that change settings or run other programs. An ask rule matches by the start of the command line, so an option placed before the command, as in project --root . init, slipped past it. Projector closed that gap with one more ask rule, Bash(project -*). But that rule also asked before project --version and project --help, which only print, and an ask rule beats both allow rules and auto mode, so every version check an agent ran prompted the person.

This pull request removes the shape the rule guarded against. project now refuses any option before its command and exits 2, so every command line it runs starts with the command and that command's own ask rule matches it. With nothing left for it to catch, Bash(project -*) leaves the rule set, and init removes it from settings that already have it.

• New commands. project version and project help [command…] replace --version and --help. The hidden --package-dir that install.sh reads becomes project version --package-dir.
  • Options move. --root and --projects-dir now follow the commands that read plans; the config subcommands take --root. review, inbox, loop, site, summary and upgrade never read either option and now refuse them.
  • Older installs. install.sh asks the installed CLI with the new command first and falls back to the old leading option, so it still reads a CLI from before this change.

cards.title: What keeps working
cards.html:
• Every command line in the shipped skills, hooks, scripts and GitHub Action already puts the command first, so none of them changes.
  • The review loop's calls parse unchanged: project review <sub> <pr> --repo … --loop … --model …, project review status <pr> --repo …, and project loop add|remove owner/repo#N --tracked <file>.
  • An installed Bash(project *) allow rule keeps matching every command. A leftover Bash(project -*) ask rule only asks before lines the CLI now refuses, and project review rules accepts settings with or without it.
  • A Codex user's projector.rules reads as outdated until project init runs again, because the allowed command list gains version and help.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Allow rule / ask rule. Entries in Claude Code's permissions.allow and permissions.ask. Claude Code checks ask rules before allow rules, and the first match decides.
  • Leading option. An option such as --root placed between project and its command.
  • Parent parser. An argparse parser whose options are copied into each parser that names it in parents=, so an option is defined once.

groups.title: The command comes first
groups.kicker: The top-level parser refuses leading options; version and help become commands
intro: The top-level parser is now CommandFirst, an argparse.ArgumentParser whose parse_known_args refuses any first word that starts with -, -- and -h included, with an error that says options go after the command and names project version and project help. It is built with add_help=False, so it takes no option at all.

--root and --projects-dir are defined once, in two parent parsers, and attached to the commands that read plans and to the config subcommands. The subcommand parsers are plain ArgumentParsers, because each of them sees its options as its first words.

checks.text: Ran the PR's CLI: project version, version --package-dir, help, help init and help review publish succeed; a leading --version, --root or -- exits 2 with the new error; project list --root . --projects-dir docs/projects lists the plans.

files.note: Swaps the top-level parser for CommandFirst, moves --root/--projects-dir into parent parsers, and adds the version and help commands.

checks.text: The refusal checks only the first word. A command's own options come after its name, and the subcommand parser that reads them is a plain ArgumentParser, so they are unaffected.

parser_class=argparse.ArgumentParser keeps every subcommand parser, and the nested review, inbox, loop, site and config parsers under it, from inheriting the refusal. Checked by parsing each review-loop command line with this head's parser.
Only the plan-reading commands and config read arguments.root or arguments.projects_dir, so dropping the options from the other commands leaves no attribute lookup behind. Checked by searching src/.
help <command…> re-parses [*topic, "--help"], so its output is exactly the command's own --help, and an unknown command exits 2 as any usage error does.

groups.title: Retiring the ask rule for a leading option
groups.kicker: Bash(project -*) leaves the rule set, and Codex allows version and help
intro: ASK loses Bash(project -*), and a new RETIRED_ASK tuple names it so init can remove it from permissions.ask, the way SUPERSEDED already removes old allow rules. When init only reports, without writing, a leftover retired rule is not counted as missing anything.
The Codex rules allow commands by name, so they never needed the ask rule. They gain help and version beside the other read-only commands.

files.note: Drops Bash(project -*) from ASK, adds RETIRED_ASK so init removes it, and adds help/version to the Codex allow list.

checks.text: Only the exact retired rule is removed; every other ask rule, including the person's own, stays in its order.

groups.title: Reading an installed CLI of either age
groups.kicker: install.sh asks with the new command and falls back to the old option
intro: install.sh status reads the installed CLI's version and package directory. Before an upgrade, that CLI can be older than the version command, so the new ask_cli function tries project version [--package-dir] first and falls back to project --version or project --package-dir.

files.note: Adds ask_cli and routes the two version reads and the package-directory read through it.

checks.text: Ran ask_cli against the installed 0.8.0 CLI, which refuses version: it fell back and printed 0.8.0 and the pipx package directory. Against this head's CLI it read version and version --package-dir directly.

groups.title: Documentation and the site
groups.kicker: Every example now puts the command first
intro: The CLI reference says the command comes first, documents project version and project help, drops Bash(project -*) from the example settings, and explains why each command's ask rule now matches every way to run it. The other pages swap project --help and project --version for the new commands.

files.note: States the command-first rule, documents version and help, and rewrites the ask-rule and Codex-rule explanations.
Names project version as the source of a review's version segment.
The site's install section shows project help.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Leading options refused, new commands, rule removal, and install fallbacks
intro: Existing tests move their leading --root and --projects-dir after the command. New tests check that every leading option, abbreviations such as --ver included, is refused before init can run; that help prints exactly what --help on the command prints; that init removes only the retired ask rule; and that install.sh status reads a fake CLI of either age.

checks.text: Ran the full suite at this head with Python 3.12: 1097 tests, OK, one skip. Also ran project check, claude plugin validate on the root and skills, claude plugin test . (144 pass), hooks/typecheck.sh, and git diff --check.
